question: Does ranking depend on the actual documentation-to-function binding when document availability and the multiset of vectors are preserved?
population: Same sorted 812 code-eligible IDs; exactly 200 nonzero-document positions and 612 zero positions retained
permutation: Python Random(seed).shuffle repeated on a copy of the sorted 200 nonzero positions until there is no fixed point, bounded to 10000 attempts; record destination-to-source map. Empty positions stay identical. Distinct IDs may still have identical vectors; report this separately.
representation: Fit original TF-IDF configuration on original sorted 2180 documents once in this batch; verify native ranking matches the parent. Reuse its vectors, vocabulary and IDF unchanged across arms; never refit per permutation.
code: Recompute frozen multiset-intersection/max-length matrix once; native code top100 must equal parent
fusion: Unchanged arithmetic mean of code and document cosine; missing document remains zero
ranking: Positive pairs only, Python round to 12 decimal places, descending score then lexicographic canonical ID pair; budget20
measurements: native overlap and exact replaced pair IDs
two post-hoc selected development anchors ranks, descriptive only
checks: no fixed points among 200 nonzero positions
document pair score multiset preserved by permutation
independent ranking and fusion arithmetic check
stop: Run all four arms once, retain all mappings and results; do not refit, choose seeds, inspect new source candidates or change budget afterwards
limits: Measures binding sensitivity, not semantic correctness or ranking quality
Not a held-out test of refactoring effectiveness
No p-value, precision or patent novelty claim
